def: A fixed program that converts text into a list of integer ids for the model and converts ids back into text.
A tokenisation method that builds a vocabulary by repeatedly merging the most frequent adjacent pair of tokens in a training text.
The ordered list of pair merges learned by byte-pair encoding, applied in that order to encode new text.
Splitting text into words, numbers and punctuation with a regular expression before merging, so that tokens do not cross those boundaries.
The encoding that turns any Unicode text into a sequence of one to four bytes per character.
Using the 256 byte values as the base alphabet so that any string can be encoded and no input is ever unknown.
A placeholder used by word-level vocabularies for any word they have never seen, which loses the word's identity.
A reserved vocabulary entry, such as an end-of-text or end-of-turn marker, that carries control meaning rather than text.
A vocabulary entry that existed in the tokeniser but was almost never seen in the model's training data, so its embedding is barely trained and it triggers odd outputs.
A subword method used by BERT that grows its vocabulary by merges chosen to raise the likelihood of the training text and marks word-internal pieces with a prefix.
A subword method that starts from a large candidate vocabulary and prunes the pieces whose removal costs least, allowing several segmentations of one word.
A library that trains BPE or unigram tokenisers directly on raw text, treating the space as an ordinary symbol.
